requirements.summary: Single recovery locus: a new Store recovery method executes once per process, after storage.Open acquires the writer lock and before startup admission (Loop.Start). It never runs in Reload, mid-run saves, or ensureReplaceable; ensureReplaceable is unchanged. [AMENDED r6: negative oracle AC1-7 added.]

Quarantinable class: any Load/LoadPrompts ErrCorrupt rejection (decode/envelope, trailing data, checksum mismatch, unsupported schema, failed Validate) and any read failure of a REGULAR file at the snapshot path are quarantinable: one atomic same-directory rename of the original file to a timestamped quarantine name before any fresh snapshot is published. Bytes are preserved exactly; no delete, truncate, or overwrite-first.

Fatal class: a non-regular file at a snapshot path (directory, device, socket — a directory cannot follow the rename rule), quarantine rename failure, and post-rename directory-sync failure are fatal: startup exits failure with code state_directory, kind resource, remediation and resource.path per the existing stateDirectoryFailure record (cmd/mcp-bridge/startup_failure.go:26-33). [AMENDED r7: single writer — serve.go's recovery block calls emitRecoveryRecords for accumulated warnings, then RETURNS stateDirectoryFailure(store.Dir()) as the error; serve never calls writeStartupFailure. runContext (cmd/mcp-bridge/main.go:59-68) is the SOLE startup_failed writer: it errors.As the returned startupFailure and writes exactly one record. This preserves AC2-4/AC2-7 one-record semantics.] The typed record is the only output for the fatal condition itself: arbitrary Go error text is never a log field or free-text line (docs/logging-contract.md); the class, kind and configured-path attribution carry the diagnosis. [AMENDED r7: this exclusivity does not suppress R4 warnings for files already quarantined earlier in the same recovery pass — AC2-7 requires warning-then-fatal.] When no rename occurred, the file is untouched; a failed rename leaves the original bytes at the original path; a failed post-rename sync leaves the bytes at the quarantine path with the original absent. startup_failure.go is NOT edited.

Typed warning: for each quarantined file exactly one structured record, event startup_snapshot_rejected, operation startup, level warn, outcome degraded, error.code snapshot_unavailable (closed AD13 mapping, docs/logging-contract.md:477), error.kind resource, error.retryable true, existing static remediation `verify the durable snapshot and storage permissions, then retry`, fixed message `startup snapshot unavailable`, resource.path = configured state directory (the resource object carries only configured path/listener/address attribution, docs/logging-contract.md:252-254, :338-340), plus two optional event-specific fields under the documented optional-addition rule (docs/logging-contract.md:499-512; schema_version stays 1): failure_reason with the finite value corrupt_json | checksum_mismatch | unsupported_schema | validation_failure | read_error, and quarantine_path = the quarantine file path. [AMENDED r6: emitted via observe.Entry{Fields} through Logger.Log (warn → stderr lane, log.go:117-133); emittability is guaranteed by the r6 T2 runtimeErrorInfo case — no `logging_write_failed` collapse, no `equivalent direct envelope build` fallback.]

Retention bound: at most 5 quarantine files per family (snapshot.corrupt-*.json, prompts.corrupt-*.json) COUNTING the file created by the current recovery. [AMENDED r7: after each successful rename, this run's file is excluded from prune candidates by exact path (a backward clock or equal timestamp can otherwise delete the just-preserved bytes, violating R2), the remaining PRE-EXISTING conforming names are ranked newest-first, and the oldest are unlinked beyond QuarantineKeep-1 — 5 pre-existing plus the new file leave exactly 5 files with the oldest pre-existing removed.] Ordering parses each name's timestamp strictly as RFC3339Nano UTC with a literal trailing `Z` (time.Parse; names matching a family glob whose timestamp is unparsable, lacks the `Z`, or carries a numeric offset, and any non-conforming directory entry, are never pruned and never counted toward the bound — foreign/operator files are never deleted). Prune failure is non-fatal and reported exactly once per AFFECTED FAMILY via a typed lifecycle record event snapshot_retention_failed, operation startup, level warn, outcome failure, error.code snapshot_unavailable, kind resource, retryable true, fixed message `quarantine retention failed`, plus quarantine_path naming the first unremoved file of that family (new AD13-table row added under the optional-addition rule; no schema_version bump). [AMENDED r6: plural `RetentionFailures` result.]

No-op on valid or absent snapshots: when Load/LoadPrompts succeeds or reports ErrNoSnapshot, recovery mutates nothing — no rename, no warning, no retention pass; a successfully loaded snapshot keeps its trusted state and the existing no-overwrite protection is untouched.

Prompt-snapshot coverage: prompts.json receives identical quarantine behavior with prompts.corrupt-*.json names, the same retention bound, the same warning record shape (quarantine_path = the prompts quarantine path), and the same read_error/rename/sync handling. [AMENDED r6: AC1-8 and AC2-9 added as full prompts oracles.]

Operator opt-out: environment variable MCP_SNAPSHOT_QUARANTINE=off (case-insensitive comparison) disables recovery (fail-closed): no quarantine rename and no new recovery record (no startup_snapshot_rejected record carrying failure_reason/quarantine_path, no snapshot_retention_failed record). Today's wedge semantics otherwise hold: the Durable loader failure still emits the pre-existing structured startup_snapshot_rejected record (internal/service/loop.go:148-151 translated by cmd/mcp-bridge/wiring.go:485-492), the admission persist fails fatally, the startup_failed/internal_error record is emitted, and the process exits 1. Any other value, including unset, enables recovery. [OWNER-CONFIRMED 2026-11-21] default = enabled. [AMENDED r7: the enabling arm is pinned by an AC2-6 enabled/1 case.]
Machine-readable reasons: Load/LoadPrompts rejections gain errors.Is-compatible reason sentinels chained under ErrCorrupt, so every existing errors.Is(err, ErrCorrupt) caller and test is unaffected.
